plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner is whoever has the highest exit price (sealed bid), and they pay the second-highest bid. In such mechanisms, bidding truthfully (your actual value) is a dominant strategy — bidding higher risks overpaying if you win, and bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Since my value is $40, I should bid exactly $40 to maximize expected profit.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit point is determined by my own sealed bid. In such mechanisms, bidding my true value is the weakly dominant strategy—it ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the price I'd pay, and never pay more than my value. Overbidding risks winning at a loss; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $13.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction (winner pays the second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value (negative profit), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Bidding my value of $17 ensures I only win when it's profitable and pay a fair price determined by others' bids.
